cithurn_00.m: You must not be from around here. If you were, you would know that it is impolite to barge into homes without invitation.
r: Sorry. I didn't mean to be rude. I'm $playername. I come from a small village where people tend to leave their doors open.

cithurn_10.m: The surrounding forest is usually quiet, but for some time now it has been under a monster invasion. I am surprised you managed to reach my home.

cithurn_100.m: Thank you. I see you are not just a great fighter, but also an adventurer that keeps his word.

cithurn_101.m: I see. You are apparently a great fighter, but not a very honorable one.

cithurn_110.m: Have you come to return my talisman?
r: Yes. I changed my mind about keeping it.
No. I already told you that I am keeping it as payment for my work.

cithurn_111.m: Thank you. It seems you do have more honor than I thought.

cithurn_112.m: Then I have nothing to say to you.

cithurn_120.m: You again? What do you want this time?
r: I wish to apologize. I'm $playername. I come from a small village where people tend to leave their doors open. I didn't mean to be rude.

cithurn_130.m: Thanks for your help, but I don't think we have anything else to discuss.

cithurn_20.m: I heard something similar was occurring in Charwood until a young adventurer killed a vile beast in the mine beneath the city.
r:
I was in Charwood recently and what you heard was true.
[You describe your experiences in Charwood and the battle with Thukuzun]
That is interesting, but I am supposed to be looking for my brother. I should leave.

cithurn_30.m: I do not know if it began happening here before the events in Charwood or after. However, from what you tell me, maybe there is a connection between the two.

cithurn_40.m: There is a cave system that runs underneath the forest. If something sinister is afoot, it could be emanating from the ground below. Please, you must help me investigate the source of the monster invasion in this forest.
r: Sorry, I cannot help you right now.
How much "investigating" will you be doing in this proposed partnership?

cithurn_50.m: Thank you. You will have to pass through the forest to reach an opening to the cave where you can enter. The opening is roughly east of my home.

cithurn_51.m: Here. Take this talisman. It does much to dispel evil forces. I acquired it long ago, and it has kept me safe over the years. Since you have agreed to help me I think your need is now greater than mine. My only request is that if you are successful, you return it to me.

cithurn_52.m: Good luck young adventurer. I await your return.

r: I killed the monster. I brought one of its bones as proof.

cithurn_61.m: Well done! A thousand thanks young adventurer. I am in your debt. However, I would still like my talisman back. I need it to keep me safe.
r: You are right about that debt. I think I'll keep the talisman as payment.

cithurn_62.m: Well $playername, you are young, and you apologized, so perhaps I will be a little forgiving. Just remember that not everywhere is like your small village. My name is Cithurn.

cithurn_64.m: What's a kid like you doing around here? It's a dangerous place to be.
r: I'm looking for my brother, Andor. He looks a bit like me.

cithurn_65.m: Sorry. I haven't seen anyone like that.
r: Thanks. Maybe I can help you with whatever is dangerous around here?
Thanks. I need to get going.
Thanks. Maybe I can help you with whatever is dangerous around here?

cithurn_66.m: I don't think so. It would need an experienced fighter to help with this problem.
r: Fine. If I'm back around here sometime in the future maybe I'll offer my help again. Or maybe I won't.

cithurn_67.m: I will clarify. A more experienced fighter than you.
r: OK. I can take a hint.

cithurn_70.m: Hmm ... I'll work on the parts that aren't dangerous. A brave and expert fighter like yourself is better suited to the dangerous parts.
r: Danger is my middle name! I'll help you.
Sorry. Flattery will not persuade me to risk my life for some piece of forest with one old man living in it.

cithurn_80.m: Well I'm the only one here. Perhaps you should leave. Come back when you have learned some manners.

cithurn_90.m: It is good to see you again $playername.
r: I explored the cave. You were correct. I found a monster called Tesrekan, which was similar to the one I found in the Charwood mine.
I think I need more help to be able to complete my mission.
I haven't found out what is happening yet, but I wanted to let you know I'm still working on it.

cithurn_91.m: OK. Thanks for keeping me updated. Please come back when you have more information.

charwood2.10: I've heard a story that the whole reason for the Charwood hills being invaded by the monsters in the first place was that something had been awoken deep in the Charwood mine. The people in the Charwood cabin say that the miners uncovered some sort of marking on the ground in a cave, with strange noises coming from below it. When they finally broke through the ground around the markings, all the troubles started. I should talk to Maevalia again.
charwood2.15: I've promised Maevalia to investigate the deeper parts of the Charwood mine. I should be on the lookout for the dangerous monsters that inhabit the mine.
charwood2.20: I've reached the part of the mine that was broken into. The air around here seems to get hotter as I get deeper into the mine.
charwood2.30: Among the fires in the lower parts of the mine, I've encountered some type of dragon-like creature. I guess this is the source of all the chaos in the mine. I should attempt to kill it and then venture back to Maevalia to tell her about it once I'm victorious.
charwood2.40: I have presented one of the bones from the corpse of the Thukuzun to Maevalia.
charwood2.50: Maevalia was happy to hear that I killed the source of the monster invasion.

waterwayacave.10: In a lonely house east of Loneford, I met an old man named Cithurn.
waterwayacave.12: Cithurn told me he needs an experienced fighter to help with his problem.
waterwayacave.15: Cithurn told me that the surrounding forest has been under invasion by monsters for several weeks.
waterwayacave.20: Cithurn heard something similar was occurring in Charwood until a young adventurer killed a vile beast in the mine beneath the city.
waterwayacave.25: I told Cithurn about my role in Charwood and of my battle with Thukuzun.
waterwayacave.30: Cithurn did not remember if the forest invasion began before the events in Charwood or after. However, based on my experiences in Charwood, Cithurn believes there is a connection between the two.
waterwayacave.35: I promised Cithurn I would investigate the source of the monster invasion in the forest. I will have to pass through the forest to access an entrance to a cave east of Cithurn's home.
waterwayacave.40: I found the entrance to the cave.
waterwayacave.45: I reached the end of the cave system. The air became damper the deeper I went.
waterwayacave.50: Among the cold and damp lower parts of the cave, I encountered another dragon-like creature. This must be the source of all the chaos in the forest above. I should attempt to kill it.
waterwayacave.55: I killed the monster called Tesrekan and took one of its bones as proof. I should venture back to Cithurn to tell him about it.
waterwayacave.60: I presented one of the bones from the corpse of Tesrekan to Cithurn. He was happy to hear that I killed the source of the monster invasion. As we agreed, I returned his talisman.
waterwayacave.70: I presented one of the bones from the corpse of Tesrekan to Cithurn. He was happy to hear that I killed the source of the monster invasion. I decided to keep his talisman as payment for my hard work.

nondisplay_2.70: Told Aemens the neighbor warned you about her
nondisplay_2.75: Taret tells you to be more careful what you say
nondisplay_2.120: Returned Cithurn's talisman after initially saying you would keep it.
nondisplay_2.180: Talked to Yolgen about the castle
nondisplay_2.220: You will never get this quest stage (used for lookout)
